# New-ZbxDashboardPage

## SYNOPSIS

Builds a dashboard page for the -Page of New-ZbxDashboard and Set-ZbxDashboard.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxDashboardPage [[-Name] <string>] [-DisplayPeriod <int>] [-Widget <ZabbixDashboardPageWidgetRequest[]>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A page holds a dashboard's widgets; a dashboard with several pages can cycle through them. The New-ZbxDashboardPage cmdlet writes it as a hashtable keyed by the API's field names, which the -Page of New-ZbxDashboard and Set-ZbxDashboard take as it is, alone or in an array. -Name is positional. Nothing is sent to the server, so the command needs no connection.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Build a page and use it in a new dashboard

```powershell
$page = New-ZbxDashboardPage -Name 'Overview' -Widget (New-ZbxDashboardWidget -Type 'clock' -Name 'Server time' -Width 12 -Height 3)
New-ZbxDashboard -Name 'Ops overview' -Page $page | Select-Object DashboardId, Name
```

The builder writes one page hashtable holding its widgets (built with New-ZbxDashboardWidget); New-ZbxDashboard sends the pages in -Page, in order.

### Example 2: A slide show of several pages

```powershell
$group = Get-ZbxHostGroup -Name 'Linux servers'
$pages = @(
    New-ZbxDashboardPage -Name 'Problems' -DisplayPeriod 60 -Widget (New-ZbxDashboardWidget -Type 'problems' -Width 72 -Height 8 -Field @{ type = 2; name = 'groupids.0'; value = $group.GroupId })
    New-ZbxDashboardPage -Name 'Clock' -DisplayPeriod 30 -Widget (New-ZbxDashboardWidget -Type 'clock' -Width 12 -Height 3)
)
$null = New-ZbxDashboard -Name 'Service status' -DisplayPeriod 60 -AutoStart $true -Page $pages
(Get-ZbxDashboard -Name 'Service status' -SelectPages).Pages | Select-Object Name, DisplayPeriod
```

-DisplayPeriod is how many seconds a page stays on screen in slide-show mode (0 = the dashboard's own period); -AutoStart starts the slide show when the dashboard opens.
